title: Surface Potential Measurement of Bacteria Using Kelvin Probe Force Microscopy
protocol: Prepare 5% sheep’s blood agar (SBA) plates for growing MRSA.
Incubate SBA plates for 24 hours at 37 °C.
Store streaked SBA plates with single colonies at 4 °C for 1 - 2 months.
Make 500 ml of tryptic soy broth (TSB) supplemented with 1% glucose and 0.1% NaCl.
Collect and clean 2 glass test tubes.
Autoclave TSB and test tubes along with a box of 1 ml pipette tips.
Pipette 5 ml of previously autoclaved TSB into autoclaved test tubes.
Wait for the TSB and test tubes to cool to room temperature.
Inoculate a single colony from a previously streaked SBA plate into 6 ml TSB broth in one test tube.
Use another test tube as a negative control to ensure sterility.
Incubate inoculated TSB test tubes at 37 °C for 24 hours in a reciprocal incubator at 200 rpm.
Pipette 1 ml from the 24-hour culture and add it to 6 ml of fresh TSB.
Incubate the mixture at 37 °C for 6 hours at 200 rpm.
Pipette 1 ml of the 6-hour subculture into a 1.5 ml microfuge tube.
Centrifuge the tube for 3 minutes at 850 x g.
Remove and discard the supernatant.
Re-suspend the pellet in 1 ml of deionized H2O.
Centrifuge again, remove and discard the supernatant.
Repeat re-suspension and centrifugation once more.
Clean stainless steel and gold AFM sample disks with 5 ml of deionized H2O on each side using forceps.
Place cleaned sample disks in a beaker containing 20 ml of deionized H2O for sonication for 1 minute.
Remove the disks from the beaker using forceps and place them at a 60° angle against the edge of an open Petri plate onto a paper towel.
Cover drying disks with the lid of the Petri plate to allow full drying, which may take between 4 - 8 hours.
Once dry, use forceps to place the sample disks into a Petri plate.
Functionalize surfaces of sample disks with poly-L-lysine for this experiment.
Pipette 200 - 400 µl of 0.1% poly-L-lysine (in H2O) onto sample disks in a Petri dish.
Incubate sample disks with poly-L-lysine at room temperature for 1 hr.
Wash sample disks with 1 ml of deionized H2O after incubation and use forceps to handle them.
Dry sample disks on paper towels.
Take re-suspended cells and plate 200 - 400 µl onto poly-L-lysine-coated sample disks in a biosafety cabinet.
Incubate cells with sample disks for 0.5 hr at room temperature if disks are coated with poly-L-lysine.
Wash sample disks gently with 1 ml of deionized H2O after incubation.
Dry sample disks overnight before imaging.
Using AFM forceps in the dominant hand, place a KPFM cantilever into the head-piece.
Hold the spring-loaded clip holder open with the subdominant hand when placing the cantilever.
Carefully load the head-piece containing the cantilever into the AFM.
Connect the appropriate wires (laser light and stage lift motor) to the AFM.
Rotate the front-to-back knob clockwise until the laser reaches the edge of the cantilever chip.
Rotate the front-to-back knob counterclockwise until the laser spot reappears on the chip’s edge.
Rotate the left-to-right knob to position the laser on the cantilever.
Turn the front-to-back knob counterclockwise to move the spot down the cantilever towards the tip until the spot disappears from the frosted glass.
Turn the front-to-back knob clockwise slightly to position the laser so that it just sits on the cantilever tip.
The laser spot will reappear on the frosted glass.
Hold the stage lift motor in the “open” position for 10 seconds.
Place the sample on the KPFM sample stage.
Ground the sample using a copper wire.
Connect the appropriate wires from the AFM to the sample stage.
Connect the stage to the AFM.
Tune the cantilever in AFM software.
Begin approach of the cantilever tip to the sample.
Set settling time at no more than 10 msec.
Ensure approach speeds do not exceed 2.0 µm/sec.
Select an imaging window size and ideal imaging area once on the sample surface.
Optimize I and P gains for topographical imaging.
Optimize cantilever set point for topographical imaging.
Turn on KPFM module in FM mode.
Use a 512 x 512 resolution with slow scan speeds of 0.02 - 0.05 lines/sec.
Set the drive percent between 5 - 10%.
Set the cantilever frequency between 1 - 5 kHz.
Set bandwidth at 2 kHz for FM-KPFM settings.
Set I and P gains for FM-KPFM settings to 0.3%.
Vary signal bandwidth and I and P gains between sample surfaces.
Further adjust signal bandwidth and I and P gains to obtain optimal images.
Process and analyze collected KPFM images using post-image processing software.
